claims.text: The driver never reached the pickup point. Under POL-NS-02 he is deemed to have arrived only where the trace holds at least 3 consecutive fixes, each at 25 m accuracy or better, inside the arrival radius for this zone class - 120 m for the LARGE_VENUE pickup at The Cascadia guardhouse recorded in EV-TRIP-00619. His own 67-fix trace contains 0 qualifying fixes: the derived arrival block reports qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0.0 seconds, and his closest approach to the pin over the entire run was 263.97 m - more than twice the radius. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails and the cancellation fee is not chargeable.

Even setting arrival aside, the waiting period the fee is paid for never ran. The effective in-geofence dwell on this trace is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second minimum for LARGE_VENUE - a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full on a shortfall 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages', and it refunds the cancellation-fee line the ledger actually charged: SGD 4.00 at EV-FARE-00619, presently sitting as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Limb (c) and limb (d) of POL-NS-01 fare no better, because the dwell never began and so the 300 seconds the fee purchases never elapsed before the 06:41:50 cancellation.

The driver's answer - 'GPS in that estate is bad' - is not available on this record, and it cuts against him either way. His trace has 100.0% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 s across 67 fixes at a 10 s cadence, so there is no degraded-signal story to tell. POL-NS-02's accuracy filter is 25 m, and no allowance the policy recognises can move a 263.97 m nearest fix inside a 120 m radius. And because POL-NS-02 makes fixes worse than 25 m evidence of neither presence nor absence, a bad-GPS plea would leave the driver with no admissible proof of arrival whatsoever.

Even on the reading most favourable to the driver - that his 263.97 m minimum distance was a stationary hold just outside the radius, which the trace does not show, since it records him moving at speeds up to 56.9 km/h across the window - POL-NS-03 gives the rider the same relief, refunding the fee 'to the rider in full'. On fault allocation under POL-NS-03 the rider's 06:36:10 message named her own position and the pin ('I'm at the front gate, the pin is the guardhouse, I can see the road and you're not here') and the driver's only answer was 'I am at your location, walk here'; the trace shows he never closed the distance before cancelling at 06:41:50. Limb (i) therefore puts the loss on the driver with no compensation, and limb (ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill is not engaged because the rider did state a sub-location.

No aggregation of dwell can rescue this fee. The only mechanism for summing separate in-geofence intervals is POL-NS-06(i), and it requires a traffic_advisory that is present, populated and covering the pickup road in the waiting window with type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. EV-ADVIS-00619-01 is MISSING - the pre-pass records 'No advisory covers the pickup road in this window' - so limb (i) is unavailable and the required 300 seconds cannot be assembled from anywhere. I cite the absent artifact for its absence, at weight 0.0.

The rider was not absent. Her own device sat at the pin for the whole waiting window: 48 qualifying fixes from 06:34:40 to 06:41:43, every one inside the 150 m rider-presence radius POL-NS-04 sets for LARGE_VENUE, mean distance 8.01 m from the pin, at 0.0 km/h throughout. The RIDER_NO_SHOW code recorded in the trip record under POL-NS-01(d) asserts an absent rider, and the rider_track contradicts that assertion on the same 10 s cadence as the driver's trace.

No driver compensation should be ordered. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it'. Limbs (b) and (c) of POL-NS-01 are not satisfied and POL-NS-06 displaces the clause outright, so the SGD 3.20 at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee is not payable. The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 is not reached on that basis; for completeness, the driver's 30-day figures - 1 no-show termination against 110 completed trips - do not trip it either, so no escalation on that ground arises.

This is a full-refund case, not a partial one, because no limb of POL-NS-08 is engaged. The 'arrived' event at 06:34:52 sits 2 seconds from the nearest trace fix at 06:34:50, far inside the 90 s skew tolerance; the trace has 100% coverage and a 0.0 s maximum gap against the 120 s threshold; the chat_log holds 2 messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 2; and the SGD 4.00 cancellation line equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under the resolution rule, so there is no fare defect. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts stands at weight 1.0, and the confidence cap in POL-GEN-02 does not bite.

I do not run POL-NS-04, and I say so rather than stretch it: the driver replied to the rider's 06:36:10 message at 06:36:40, 30 seconds later and well inside the 120 s window, and had already placed an answered 110-second in-app call at 06:35:40, so limbs (a) and (b) cannot hold and the clause does not exonerate the rider on its own terms. That costs the rider nothing, because the fee falls on the arrival and dwell failures under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06, and POL-NS-06 refunds the fee whether or not the rider responded to messages. A driver who communicates diligently still cannot charge for a wait that never happened.

claims.text: POL-NS-04 is not available to the rider on this record. The rider's locating message was sent at 06:36:10 and the driver replied at 06:36:40, thirty seconds later and comfortably inside the clause's 120 second window; independently, the driver had already placed an in-app voice call at 06:35:40 which the trip record shows was answered and ran 110 seconds, i.e. to about 06:37:30, well before the 06:41:50 termination. Limb (b) fails on either branch, so the rider cannot be exonerated under this clause.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival provision does not reach this driver. His closest recorded fix is 264 m from the pin - outside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, but inside the 300 m line - and the clause says in terms that a driver who is stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius when marking arrival is not caught by it and is decided under POL-NS-03. The trip should therefore not be recorded as a false-arrival event against him.

This is the wrong-entrance fact pattern of POL-NS-03, not a rider no-show. The pickup was a large-venue zone carrying two registered pickup points; the rider's device sat within about 8 m of the pin, stationary, across all 48 of her qualifying fixes, while the driver's closest approach was 264 m - inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling and never inside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius. The two parties were at different faces of the pickup zone, and the record therefore decides this cancellation under POL-NS-03.

Fault should be attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to the driver, and the driver should receive the POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill. The zone carries two registered pickup points; neither message designated which of them to use - the rider's message said where she was standing and that the pin itself sat at the guardhouse, so nothing in the chat establishes that the 'front gate' she named was the correct pickup entrance he should have moved to - and the driver was on the phone with her for 110 seconds trying to close the gap before he cancelled. On those facts POL-NS-03(ii) applies and the driver is owed the platform-funded goodwill of 50 percent of the cancellation fee, SGD 2.00 of the SGD 4.00 charged, which is charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider.

ruling.explanation:
Both parties' surviving points are answered here. The charge is the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee on EV-FARE-00619, levied on a driver-cancelled RIDER_NO_SHOW.

The controlling finding is that the driver never reached the pickup point. Under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived only where the GPS trace holds at least 3 consecutive fixes, each accurate to 25 m or better, inside the arrival radius for the zone class. This pickup is a LARGE_VENUE (EV-TRIP-00619, The Cascadia guardhouse), so the radius is 120 m. The driver's own 67-fix trace (EV-GPS-00619) contains zero qualifying in-geofence fixes — qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying run of 0.0 seconds — and his closest recorded approach was 263.97 m, more than twice the radius. POL-NS-01 limb (b) fails and the fee is not chargeable.

Independently, POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation-fee line for a waiting-period shortfall: the effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second LARGE_VENUE minimum, a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. That clause refunds the fee whether or not the rider was present or responded, so the rider's response does not matter to the refund.

I reject the driver's account that this was bad GPS and a wrong-face-of-the-venue case under POL-NS-03. The trace has 100% coverage, no gaps and a 0.0 s maximum gap across 67 fixes at a 10 s cadence, so there is no degraded-signal story to tell, and no accuracy allowance the policy recognises moves a 263.97 m fix inside a 120 m radius. POL-NS-03 does not engage at all: it requires the driver to have been stationary for the required dwell at a point within 400 m of the pin, and the trace shows no such hold — the driver was moving at speeds up to 56.9 km/h. The driver's request for the POL-NS-03(ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill of SGD 2.00 therefore fails at the predicate; in any event the rider's 06:36:10 message named her own position and the pin, which is the limb (i) situation, not limb (ii).

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 both displace it, so the SGD 3.20 figure (80% of SGD 4.00) is never reached, and the anti-farming check is not reached either.

The driver's further point that POL-NS-05's false-arrival provision does not catch him is accepted on this record: his closest recorded approach, 263.97 m, sits inside the clause's 300 m line, and the record does not fix his speed at the 06:34:52 arrival timestamp. No false-arrival record is entered against him, and no referral is produced.

The rider's POL-NS-04 point is accepted but immaterial: the driver replied at 06:36:40, 30 seconds after the rider's message, and had already placed an answered 110-second in-app call at 06:35:40, so limb (b) of that clause cannot hold on its own terms. Her device nonetheless sat at the pin throughout — 48 qualifying fixes from 06:34:40 to 06:41:43, mean 8.01 m, at 0.0 km/h — so the RIDER_NO_SHOW code's premise of an absent rider is contradicted by the same trace on the same 10 s cadence.

On confidence I check POL-NS-08 and find no limb engaged: the 'arrived' event at 06:34:52 sits two seconds from the nearest fix (well inside the 90 s skew tolerance), the trace has no gap over 120 s and 67 fixes, the chat_log holds exactly the 2 messages trip_record.chat_message_count records, and the SGD 4.00 line equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under the fee_schedule resolution rule — no fare defect. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts stands at weight 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap does not bite and the case does not escalate under POL-NS-09.

Result: the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full, no driver compensation is payable, and the charge on EV-FARE-00619 is reversed.

ruling.explanation:
Decision on trip TRP-00619 (The Cascadia guardhouse to Woodlands Checkpoint). The contested no-show fee of SGD 4.00 is refunded to the rider in full, and no driver compensation is payable.

Why the charge falls. The platform's own GPS trace (EV-GPS-00619, weight 1.00) holds 67 driver fixes at 100% coverage; not one of them falls inside the 120 m arrival radius for this LARGE_VENUE pickup (qualifying_fix_count 0), and the driver's closest approach to the pin was 263.97 m. Under POL-NS-02 the driver is deemed to have arrived only on at least three consecutive in-radius fixes at 25 m accuracy or better; there are none, so POL-NS-01(b) fails and the fee is not chargeable. Independently, the effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 s against the 300 s minimum for LARGE_VENUE — a shortfall of 300.0 s — so POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages. The rider was in fact at the pin throughout (her rider track: 48 qualifying fixes, mean 8.01 m, stationary), so the RIDER_NO_SHOW code in EV-TRIP-00619 (weight 1.00) is contradicted by the platform's own telemetry.

On the driver's arguments. (1) 'GPS in that estate is bad' does not survive: the trace has 100% coverage, a maximum gap of 0.0 s, and no allowance the policy recognises can move a 263.97 m nearest fix inside 120 m; and because fixes worse than 25 m count as evidence of neither presence nor absence, a bad-GPS plea would leave no admissible proof of arrival at all. (2) I accept your wrong-entrance framing. Your trace shows you held position for the waiting window at about 264 m from the pin — outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling — and 264 m is inside the 300 m line, so POL-NS-05 does not catch you and POL-NS-03 governs rather than a false-arrival finding. But POL-NS-03 still refunds this fee to the rider in full. (3) Your request for the pin-ambiguity goodwill (50% of the fee, SGD 2.00) is refused. Fault is allocated from the chat log (EV-CHAT-00619): the rider's 06:36:10 message stated her position and the pin ('I'm at the front gate, the pin is the guardhouse') and you did not move to it before cancelling at 06:41:50. That engages POL-NS-03(i) — you bear the loss and receive no compensation — and limb (ii) is not engaged because a sub-location was stated. (4) You are right that POL-NS-04 does not apply to the rider: you replied 30 seconds after her message (inside the 120 s window) and had already placed an answered 110-second in-app call at 06:35:40. That clause does not exonerate her on its own terms, but it costs her nothing, because the fee falls on the arrival and dwell failures.

No driver compensation under POL-NS-07 either: it pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limbs (b) and (c) are not. The anti-farming check is not reached, and the driver's 30-day figures (1 no-show termination against 110 completed trips) would not trip it in any event.

Integrity and escalation. No limb of POL-NS-08 is engaged: the 'arrived' event at 06:34:52 sits 2 s from the nearest fix at 06:34:50 (inside the 90 s tolerance); the trace has no gap above 120 s; the chat log's 2 messages match the trip record's chat_message_count of 2; and the SGD 4.00 cancellation line equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under the resolution rule. So there is no basis for a partial refund. Nor for escalation: confidence (0.90) is above the 0.70 floor; no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the counterparty-dispute counters are 0; and no abuse trigger fires. The missing traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00619-01 (weight 0.00) affects only the POL-NS-06(i) accumulation route, which changes nothing because the full refund already follows.

Figures used: contested amount SGD 4.00; fee charged SGD 4.00; refund SGD 4.00. The goodwill figure of SGD 2.00 and the compensation figure of SGD 3.20 do not apply.

Independently, the effective in-geofence dwell is 0.0 s against the 300 s minimum for LARGE_VENUE — a shortfall of 300.0 s — so POL-NS-06 refunds the fee in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not she replied to messages. On the driver's arguments. (1) 'GPS in that estate is bad' does not survive: the trace has 100% coverage, a maximum gap of 0.0 s, and no allowance the policy recognises can move a 263.97 m nearest fix inside 120 m; and because fixes worse than 25 m count as evidence of neither presence nor absence, a bad-GPS plea would leave no admissible proof of arrival at all. (2) I accept your wrong-entrance framing. Your trace shows you held position for the waiting window at about 264 m from the pin — outside the 120 m arrival radius but inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling — and 264 m is inside the 300 m line, so POL-NS-05 does not catch you and POL-NS-03 governs rather than a false-arrival finding. But POL-NS-03 still refunds this fee to the rider in full. (3) Your request for the pin-ambiguity goodwill (50% of the fee, SGD 2.00) is refused. Fault is allocated from the chat log (EV-CHAT-00619): the rider's 06:36:10 message stated her position and the pin ('I'm at the front gate, the pin is the guardhouse') and you did not move to it before cancelling at 06:41:50. That engages POL-NS-03(i) — you bear the loss and receive no compensation — and limb (ii) is not engaged because a sub-location was stated. (4) You are right that POL-NS-04 does not apply to the rider: you replied 30 seconds after her message (inside the 120 s window) and had already placed an answered 110-second in-app call at 06:35:40. That clause does not exonerate her on its own terms, but it costs her nothing, because the fee falls on the arrival and dwell failures.

No driver compensation under POL-NS-07 either: it pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and limbs (b) and (c) are not. The anti-farming check is not reached, and the driver's 30-day figures (1 no-show termination against 110 completed trips) would not trip it in any event.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: the dispute is over the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee charged to the rider (EV-FARE-00619: cancellation_fee 4.00, total_charged 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00). That fee is refunded in full.

The charge cannot stand under POL-NS-01, which needs all four limbs. Limb (b) requires the GPS trace to place the driver inside the pickup geofence — 120 m for this LARGE_VENUE pickup at The Cascadia guardhouse — at or before the 06:34:52 'arrived' event. The driver's own 67-fix trace (EV-GPS-00619, weight 1.0) reports 0 qualifying in-geofence fixes (qualifying_fix_count 0) and a closest approach of 263.97 m, more than twice the radius. Limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 300 s; the measured dwell is 0.0 s, a shortfall of 300.0 s. With limbs (b) and (c) failing, POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06 each direct a full refund, and POL-NS-06 refunds the fee 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages' — so neither the rider's presence (48 qualifying fixes, mean 8.01 m from the pin, stationary) nor the driver's reply and 110-second answered call rescues the charge.

The driver's account that 'GPS in that estate is bad' is not available on this record: EV-GPS-00619 has 100.0% coverage, no gaps and a 0.0 s maximum gap, and the 25 m accuracy filter cannot move a 263.97 m nearest fix inside a 120 m radius.

On the wrong-entrance argument: the pickup carried 2 registered pickup points and the driver's closest approach of 263.97 m sits inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling, so POL-NS-03 governs the fault allocation — and it gives the rider the same full refund. The driver's claim for the pin-ambiguity goodwill (SGD 2.00, 50% of the SGD 4.00 fee) is rejected: limb (ii) applies only where NEITHER party specified a sub-location, and the rider's 06:36:10 message named where she was ('I'm at the front gate, the pin is the guardhouse'). Under limb (i) the rider gave a locating statement and the driver did not move to it before cancelling at 06:41:50, so the driver bears the loss and receives no compensation.

No driver compensation is payable. POL-NS-07 pays only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it; it is not satisfied, and POL-NS-06 displaces it. (For completeness the anti-farming check does not trip: 1 no-show termination in 30 days against 110 completed trips.)

No POL-NS-08 impairment arises, so this is a full refund and not a partial one: the 06:34:52 arrival event is 2 s from the nearest fix (inside the 90 s skew tolerance); the trace has no gap over 120 s; the chat holds 2 messages matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 2; and the SGD 4.00 line equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00). The deciding facts rest on artifacts at weight 1.0, so the confidence cap is 1.0. The MISSING traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00619-01, weight 0.0) matters only to POL-NS-06(i) aggregation, which is not reached because there is no in-geofence interval to sum.

The rider's separate POL-NS-04 claim is not needed and was correctly not pressed: the driver replied within 120 s and had already called, so that clause does not exonerate her; the refund comes from the arrival and dwell failures. The driver's POL-NS-05 point is accepted — the closest fix (263.97 m) is inside the 300 m line, so the arrival marker is not shown to be false and no false-arrival referral is recorded. No clause produces a referral here, and no escalation ground is met (confidence is above the 0.70 floor, the profiles show 0 cross-party disputes and 0 relevant counters, and the trace is unimpaired). One rider claim was discarded at the citation stage for not disclosing the missing advisory's impairment, and nothing is built on it.

EV-ADVIS-00619-01 is MISSING - the pre-pass records 'No advisory covers the pickup road in this window' - so limb (i) is unavailable and the required 300 seconds cannot be assembled from anywhere. ledger.claim: The driver never reached the pickup point. Under POL-NS-02 he is deemed to have arrived only where the trace holds at least 3 consecutive fixes, each at 25 m accuracy or better, inside the arrival radius for this zone class - 120 m for the LARGE_VENUE pickup at The Cascadia guardhouse recorded in EV-TRIP-00619. His own 67-fix trace contains 0 qualifying fixes: the derived arrival block reports qualifying_fix_count 0 and a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 0.0 seconds, and his closest approach to the pin over the entire run was 263.97 m - more than twice the radius. POL-NS-01 limb (b) therefore fails and the cancellation fee is not chargeable.

Even setting arrival aside, the waiting period the fee is paid for never ran. The effective in-geofence dwell on this trace is 0.0 seconds against the 300-second minimum for LARGE_VENUE - a shortfall of 300.0 seconds. POL-NS-06 refunds the cancellation fee in full on a shortfall 'whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages', and it refunds the cancellation-fee line the ledger actually charged: SGD 4.00 at EV-FARE-00619, presently sitting as CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00. Limb (c) and limb (d) of POL-NS-01 fare no better, because the dwell never began and so the 300 seconds the fee purchases never elapsed before the 06:41:50 cancellation.

The driver's answer - 'GPS in that estate is bad' - is not available on this record, and it cuts against him either way. His trace has 100.0% coverage, no gaps at all and a maximum gap of 0.0 s across 67 fixes at a 10 s cadence, so there is no degraded-signal story to tell. POL-NS-02's accuracy filter is 25 m, and no allowance the policy recognises can move a 263.97 m nearest fix inside a 120 m radius. And because POL-NS-02 makes fixes worse than 25 m evidence of neither presence nor absence, a bad-GPS plea would leave the driver with no admissible proof of arrival whatsoever.

Even on the reading most favourable to the driver - that his 263.97 m minimum distance was a stationary hold just outside the radius, which the trace does not show, since it records him moving at speeds up to 56.9 km/h across the window - POL-NS-03 gives the rider the same relief, refunding the fee 'to the rider in full'. On fault allocation under POL-NS-03 the rider's 06:36:10 message named her own position and the pin ('I'm at the front gate, the pin is the guardhouse, I can see the road and you're not here') and the driver's only answer was 'I am at your location, walk here'; the trace shows he never closed the distance before cancelling at 06:41:50. Limb (i) therefore puts the loss on the driver with no compensation, and limb (ii) pin-ambiguity goodwill is not engaged because the rider did state a sub-location.

No aggregation of dwell can rescue this fee. The only mechanism for summing separate in-geofence intervals is POL-NS-06(i), and it requires a traffic_advisory that is present, populated and covering the pickup road in the waiting window with type KERB_RESTRICTION, ENFORCEMENT, CLOSURE or ACCIDENT. EV-ADVIS-00619-01 is MISSING - the pre-pass records 'No advisory covers the pickup road in this window' - so limb (i) is unavailable and the required 300 seconds cannot be assembled from anywhere. I cite the absent artifact for its absence, at weight 0.0.

ledger.claim: The rider was not absent. Her own device sat at the pin for the whole waiting window: 48 qualifying fixes from 06:34:40 to 06:41:43, every one inside the 150 m rider-presence radius POL-NS-04 sets for LARGE_VENUE, mean distance 8.01 m from the pin, at 0.0 km/h throughout. The RIDER_NO_SHOW code recorded in the trip record under POL-NS-01(d) asserts an absent rider, and the rider_track contradicts that assertion on the same 10 s cadence as the driver's trace.

No driver compensation should be ordered. POL-NS-07 pays the driver only 'where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full and no clause from POL-NS-03 to POL-NS-06 displaces it'. Limbs (b) and (c) of POL-NS-01 are not satisfied and POL-NS-06 displaces the clause outright, so the SGD 3.20 at 80 percent of the SGD 4.00 fee is not payable. The anti-farming check under POL-NS-07 is not reached on that basis; for completeness, the driver's 30-day figures - 1 no-show termination against 110 completed trips - do not trip it either, so no escalation on that ground arises.

This is a full-refund case, not a partial one, because no limb of POL-NS-08 is engaged. The 'arrived' event at 06:34:52 sits 2 seconds from the nearest trace fix at 06:34:50, far inside the 90 s skew tolerance; the trace has 100% coverage and a 0.0 s maximum gap against the 120 s threshold; the chat_log holds 2 messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count of 2; and the SGD 4.00 cancellation line equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone fee (SGD 4.00) and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee (SGD 4.00) under the resolution rule, so there is no fare defect. Every artifact carrying the deciding facts stands at weight 1.0, and the confidence cap in POL-GEN-02 does not bite.

I do not run POL-NS-04, and I say so rather than stretch it: the driver replied to the rider's 06:36:10 message at 06:36:40, 30 seconds later and well inside the 120 s window, and had already placed an answered 110-second in-app call at 06:35:40, so limbs (a) and (b) cannot hold and the clause does not exonerate the rider on its own terms. That costs the rider nothing, because the fee falls on the arrival and dwell failures under POL-NS-01, POL-NS-02 and POL-NS-06, and POL-NS-06 refunds the fee whether or not the rider responded to messages. A driver who communicates diligently still cannot charge for a wait that never happened.

POL-NS-04 is not available to the rider on this record. The rider's locating message was sent at 06:36:10 and the driver replied at 06:36:40, thirty seconds later and comfortably inside the clause's 120 second window; independently, the driver had already placed an in-app voice call at 06:35:40 which the trip record shows was answered and ran 110 seconds, i.e. to about 06:37:30, well before the 06:41:50 termination. Limb (b) fails on either branch, so the rider cannot be exonerated under this clause.

POL-NS-05's false-arrival provision does not reach this driver. His closest recorded fix is 264 m from the pin - outside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, but inside the 300 m line - and the clause says in terms that a driver who is stationary within 300 m of the pin but outside the arrival radius when marking arrival is not caught by it and is decided under POL-NS-03. The trip should therefore not be recorded as a false-arrival event against him.

This is the wrong-entrance fact pattern of POL-NS-03, not a rider no-show. The pickup was a large-venue zone carrying two registered pickup points; the rider's device sat within about 8 m of the pin, stationary, across all 48 of her qualifying fixes, while the driver's closest approach was 264 m - inside POL-NS-03's 400 m ceiling and never inside the POL-NS-02 arrival radius. The two parties were at different faces of the pickup zone, and the record therefore decides this cancellation under POL-NS-03.

Fault should be attributed to pin ambiguity rather than to the driver, and the driver should receive the POL-NS-03(ii) goodwill. The zone carries two registered pickup points; neither message designated which of them to use - the rider's message said where she was standing and that the pin itself sat at the guardhouse, so nothing in the chat establishes that the 'front gate' she named was the correct pickup entrance he should have moved to - and the driver was on the phone with her for 110 seconds trying to close the gap before he cancelled. On those facts POL-NS-03(ii) applies and the driver is owed the platform-funded goodwill of 50 percent of the cancellation fee, SGD 2.00 of the SGD 4.00 charged, which is charged to the platform and never recovered from the rider.
